speaker_role: independent college admissions strategist/consultant (~30 years experience; former college readiness coordinator, assistant principal, and English teacher)
commercial_incentive: Heavily promotes her paid 'Admissions Formula' course and 'College List Building Masterclass' throughout
key_insights: High school counselor caseloads often exceed 400 students, and most one-on-one counselor meetings don't happen until second semester of junior year

High schools vary between 'gatekeeping' (strict prerequisites, no exceptions) and 'gateway' (open enrollment via waivers) course-placement philosophies, which affects what a counselor can flexibly offer

Many high school counselors have little formal college-admissions training, since a large share of their role covers testing administration, scheduling, and emotional counseling rather than college advising
Recommends parents/students define a clear purpose and question list before each counselor meeting, since meeting time is very limited

Strong counselor letters of recommendation are said to come from students personally initiating contact and self-advocating, rather than from parent-completed surveys the counselor then 'regurgitates'
Students should learn their school's course drop deadline in advance so they can level up or down without risking an F on the transcript
Recommends asking counselors for a multi-year ('horizontal') course plan rather than just next year's classes, to avoid missing prerequisites for future rigor
specific_numbers_or_facts: Counselor caseloads cited as 'upwards of 400+' students on the low end (per Lisa McLaughlin)
notable_or_distinctive: Frames the counselor-student relationship itself (proactive student emailing, self-advocacy) as the actual mechanism that produces strong recommendation letters, illustrated with a detailed personal anecdote about her own daughter.
reliability_notes: Heavy promotional content for a paid course; claims about counselor training and caseloads are asserted from personal experience without citation; transcript has some rambling typical of live unscripted video.
